messages:
Ryan: paging — seeing a pretty bad perf cliff on kv-cache in us-west-2. latency p95 jumped ~4-8x, a few workers hit cudaMalloc OOMs. IncidentBot fired earlier. Root TS 1742001234
IncidentBot: AUTOMATED ALERT: Elevated error rate and memory alloc failures for service=kv-cache, pool=dedicated-usw2. severity=2. notified: @ryan, @maya.
Maya: oncall taking — will triage. quick question: is this the continuous-batching path or the on-demand small-batch resending?
Ryan: looks tied to continuous-batching. graphs show sharp increase in active KV items and eviction churn. suspect fragmentation -> allocator regressions after sustained load spike.
Sriram: adding context — we pushed a quant change last week that increased item sizes slightly; continuous batching interleaves many small KV updates which may create many small CUDA allocations and then frees. cudaMalloc + cudaFree churn can fragment the device arena.
Alex: seeing the same in logs. pasted a snippet:
```
[2025-03-11T09:14:02Z] ERROR worker-7: cuda runtime error (2) : out of memory at /pytorch/aten/src/THC/THCGeneral.cpp:86
[2025-03-11T09:14:02Z] WARN batcher: failed to allocate 131072 bytes (0.125 MB) for kv item
```
Jen: customer-impact: a few Dedicated customers reported 503s on embed endpoints around 09:12-09:18 UTC. Support is fielding tickets, estimated affected percentage ~2% of requests routed to those pools.
Maya: immediate mitigation plan — 1) temporarily disable continuous batching on the affected pool, 2) reduce max_batch_size on the runtime to 32, 3) apply malloc/arena env mitigations on workers, 4) gracefully drain and restart workers one AZ at a time.
Alex: applying batcher hotfix now. patch via runtime config API:
```
PATCH /v1/internal/config/batcher
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "pool":"dedicated-usw2",
  "continuous_batching": false,
  "max_batch_size": 32
}
```
Alex: patch accepted, rollout started to 6/6 proxies. turning off continuous-batching for dedicated-usw2.
Sriram: parallel mitigation — set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF and MALLOC_ARENA_MAX on workers to reduce GPU fragmentation:
```
export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
export MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1
systemctl restart redwood-kv-worker
```
Sriram: on some hosts old glibc arenas + cuda caching allocator cause fragmentation. MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 helps coalesce host-side heaps. max_split_size_mb lowers split threshold and reduces tiny cuda allocations.
Alex: rolling restarts in progress, batcher disabled reduced tail latency almost immediately on first hosts. p95 down from 1.2s to ~220ms on restarted nodes.
Jen: notifying affected customers: emailed two Dedicated customers with short mitigation note and ETA for full fix.
Ryan: monitoring — dashboards show error rate trending down but still some residual OOM spikes on older hosts that haven't restarted.
Maya: handoff — I'll take lead for the next hour to watch rollouts and coordinate postmortem. Ryan handing off now. @Ryan -> @Maya.
Ryan: thanks. docs: I posted short incident summary to #incidents. Next steps for RCA: collect malloc/free histograms, nvprof traces from affected windows, and correlate with eviction churn metrics.
Sriram: initial hypothesis for RCA: KV cache fragmentation caused by high churn of variable-sized values + allocator change in pytorch runtime exposing a regression in cudaMalloc behavior. Possible lines of remediation: 1) move to a persistent memory pool allocator for KV cache buffers, 2) upstream PyTorch upgrade with allocator fixes, 3) systematic cap on per-shard insertion rate + better eviction smoothing.
Alex: file a quick follow-up ticket for a longer-term fix: 'kv-cache: implement pooled GPU allocator + test under churn' and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml.
Maya: action items captured: [hotfix applied, env mitigations rolled, rolling restarts underway, customer comms sent]. I'll keep this thread updated with final numbers and timeline to full recovery.
Jen: support will keep customers updated and collect more user-side logs; escalate if more than 5% requests still failing.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated (partial), impacted_customers=2, s0_approx=false.
Maya: marking handoff done. planning a 1-hour follow-up bridge at 10:20 UTC for RCA planning.
Ryan: thanks team. postmortem owners: Maya (lead), Sriram (allocator analysis), Alex (runtime changes), Jen (customer comms).
Maya: adding final note — if anyone sees recurring OOMs after restarts, ping me directly and we'll revert the quant change we rolled last week as a temporary rollback.
